claims.text: Controlled TiH2 decomposition under ultra-high vacuum and a specified heating-rate profile suppresses nucleation of brittle Ti-rich alpha-HCP phases by lowering oxygen content.
Suppressing oxygen uptake and alpha-HCP nucleation enables production of a dense, crack-free bulk refractory high-entropy alloy.
Coherent BCC/B2 precipitation enhances high-temperature yield strength.
TiH2 acts as an oxygen scavenger during processing.
Hydrogen supplied by TiH2 causes lattice expansion during powder compaction.
A slow ramp of 1–2 °C/min to 400–500 °C, with a two-hour hold, is required for controlled TiH2 decomposition.
Rapid heating to 1100–1200 °C followed by extrusion at greater than 1 GPa for less than 10 minutes densifies the alloy without catastrophic cracking.
The decomposition stage requires ultra-high vacuum below 10^-6 Pa or an inert atmosphere with active gettering.
Hydrogen released by TiH2 reacts with dissolved oxygen to form H2O that can be evacuated under vacuum.
Residual oxygen is removed as volatile TiO and/or H2O during hydride decomposition.
Oxygen removal below a critical concentration prevents alpha-HCP precipitation.
High hydrostatic extrusion pressure suppresses void formation and promotes solid-state diffusion and BCC-matrix homogenization.
The proposed thermal cycle promotes fine coherent BCC/B2 precipitates while avoiding brittle Laves and silicide phases.
The process produces a bulk alloy with greater than 98% relative density and no catastrophic cracking.
The final microstructure is single-phase BCC or dual-phase BCC/B2 and contains no alpha-HCP phase.
The processed alloy has a yield strength exceeding 400 MPa at 1600 °C.
In HEAP-S HfNbTaTiZr, approximately 0.75 wt% oxygen was associated with brittleness and radial cracking during hot swaging.
Oxygen introduced during processing of NbMoTaWVTi can produce FCC TiO precipitates in a BCC matrix.
The proposed method is limited to Group IV-containing alloys susceptible to hydride formation and oxygen embrittlement.
Oxygen removal can become kinetically limited when initial oxygen content is sufficiently high or hydride decomposition occurs above the densification temperature.

contradictions.description: The proposed initial alloy contains W, V, Ta, Ti, and Cr, whereas the falsification experiment tests NbMoTaWVTi. The experiment therefore changes the base alloy by replacing Cr with Nb and Mo and does not directly test the stated material system.
